runs.t: La voiture est ici. Elle est rouge.

comment: The car is here. It is red.
replaces the feminine noun
, not a female person.

detail.label: Polite singular

runs.t: Vous êtes prête, Madame ?

comment: Are you ready, madam? Polite singular
takes the
verb form but feminine singular
for this addressee.

detail.label: Three readings of the generic subject

runs.t: On part à huit heures. En France, on conduit à droite. On frappe à la porte.

comment: We leave at eight [our group]. In France, people drive on the right. Someone is knocking. The context selects the referent.

detail.label: Known referents

runs.t: Avec Léa, on est arrivées tôt.

comment: Léa and I arrived early [both feminine].
keeps a singular verb, but adjective/participle agreement can reflect known referents.

detail.label: First-person elision

runs.t: J'arrive. Je pars.

comment: I’m arriving. I’m leaving.
becomes
before a vowel; it does not simply disappear.

detail.label: Address choice
runs: Use

runs.t: vous

runs: for polite distance or several people. Familiar

runs.t: tu

runs: is common with friends and family; changing the relationship is a social decision, not a translation of English “you”.

stressed.title: Me, him, us: stressed pronouns
stressed.lead: Use stressed pronouns after many prepositions, for emphasis and in coordinated subjects. They are different from pre-verb object pronouns.

detail.label: Emphasis

runs.t: Moi, je reste ici. Et toi ?

comment: As for me, I’m staying here. And you?
adds emphasis;
is the ordinary subject.

detail.label: Short identification

runs.t: Qui est là ? C'est moi.

comment: Who is there? It’s me. French uses stressed
after

detail.label: Coordination

runs.t: Toi et moi, nous sommes prêts.

comment: You and I are ready [masculine/mixed]. The coordinated subject has first-person plural agreement.

detail.label: Complement frame

runs.t: Je pense à lui. Je lui parle.

comment: I’m thinking about him. I’m speaking to him.
a person keeps a stressed pronoun;
uses the indirect clitic.

detail.label: Comparison

runs.t: Elle est plus grande que moi.

comment: She is taller than I am. Stressed
follows
in this comparison.

question-patterns.title: Yes/no questions
question-patterns.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: English do/does has no equivalent auxiliary here. Use statement order with question intonation,

runs.t: est-ce que

runs: , or formal inversion.

detail.label: Vowel and -t-

runs.t: Est-ce qu'elle arrive ? Arrive-t-elle ?

comment: Is she arriving? In third-person inversion add -t- with
before
; not when the verb already ends in t/d.

detail.label: Noun subject

runs.t: Léa vient-elle ?

comment: Is Léa coming? Formal inversion retains the noun and adds a corresponding pronoun.

detail.label: Compound verb

runs.t: Avez-vous réservé ?

comment: Have you booked? Invert the conjugated auxiliary, not

detail.label: Negative inversion

runs.t: N'avez-vous pas réservé ?

comment: Haven’t you booked?
comes before the auxiliary and
after the subject pronoun.

detail.label: Existence

runs.t: Y a-t-il une place ?

comment: Is there a seat? Recognize the inverted
frame.

detail.label: Register
runs: Statement-order questions are common in speech.

runs.t: est-ce que

runs: is a useful neutral explicit pattern; inversion is more formal. These are choices of form/register, not different yes/no meanings.

question-words.title: Who, what, where, which?
question-words.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Ask for the missing role. People and things have distinct subject/object question patterns;

runs.t: quel

runs: agrees with its noun.

detail.label: Identification

runs.t: Qui est-ce ? Qu'est-ce que c'est ?

comment: Who is it? What is it? These ask for a person’s or thing’s identity.

detail.label: Missing subject or object

runs.t: Qu’est-ce qui fait ce bruit ? Qu’est-ce que tu fais ?

comment: What is making that noise? What are you doing? First question has no separate subject

detail.label: Which/what: agreement

runs.t: Quelle heure est-il ? Quelles places restent libres ?

comment: What time is it? Which seats remain free?
is feminine singular;
feminine plural.

detail.label: After a preposition

runs.t: Avec qui viens-tu ? De quoi parlez-vous ?

comment: Who are you coming with? What are you talking about? Keep the French preposition before

detail.label: Conversational position

runs.t: Tu pars quand ?

comment: When are you leaving? Question word can remain at the end in conversation.

detail.label: Which one — recognition

runs.t: Il y a deux trains. Lequel prends-tu ?

comment: There are two trains. Which one are you taking?
stands without a following noun;
agree with the referent [feminine singular / masculine plural / feminine plural].

basic-negation.title: Not & never: the basic frame
basic-negation.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Standard written negation uses

runs.t: ne
n’

runs: before the finite verb and

runs.t: pas

runs: or

runs.t: jamais

runs: after it. There is no English do-support.

detail.label: With a pronoun

runs.t: Je ne le vois pas. Elle ne se lève jamais tard.

comment: I don’t see him/it. She never gets up late.

detail.label: Infinitive

runs.t: Je préfère ne pas partir.

comment: I prefer not to leave. With a negative infinitive,
precedes the infinitive.

detail.label: Conversational recognition

runs.t: Je sais pas. J'ai pas le temps.

comment: I don’t know. I don’t have time. Familiar spoken forms omit
; they are not the standard written templates taught here.

detail.label: Article consequence

runs.t: Je n'ai pas de billet. Ce n'est pas un billet.

comment: I don’t have a ticket. It isn’t a ticket. Indefinite amount often becomes
, but not automatically after

detail.label: Reply to a negative question

runs.t: Tu ne viens pas ? — Si, je viens.

comment: Aren’t you coming? — Yes, I am.
contradicts the negative assumption.

negative-choices.title: Nothing, nobody, only, neither
negative-choices.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Replace

runs.t: pas

runs: with the negative word needed by your meaning. A negative word can also be the subject. Restrictive

runs.t: ne…que

runs: means only.

detail.label: Compound positions

runs.t: Je n'ai rien vu. Je n'ai vu personne.

comment: I saw nothing. I saw nobody.
precedes the participle;
follows it.

detail.label: Negative subject

runs.t: Rien ne change. Aucun train ne part.

comment: Nothing changes. No train leaves. The negative subject goes first;
remains before the verb.

detail.label: Not a single: agreement

runs.t: Je n'ai aucune idée.

comment: I have no idea.
is feminine singular, giving
; plural lexical exceptions are outside this basic pattern.

detail.label: Neither nor

runs.t: Je ne bois ni café ni thé.

comment: I drink neither coffee nor tea. This ordinary general-quantity
frame omits the partitive articles.

detail.label: Restriction scope

runs.t: Je ne travaille que le lundi. Je n'ai que deux billets.

comment: I work only on Mondays. I have only two tickets.
introduces the restricted expression.

detail.label: No longer

runs.t: Je ne travaille plus ici.

comment: I no longer work here. In spoken forms without
, context and pronunciation can distinguish negative
from positive “more”.

presentatives.title: Identify, describe or introduce
presentatives.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Separate identification, description and existence. A noun phrase introduced with

runs.t: c’est

runs: differs from an adjective describing an identified referent.

detail.label: Noun phrase versus attribute

runs.t: C'est une bonne idée. Elle est bonne.

comment: It’s a good idea. It is good [the idea].
introduces a determined noun phrase;
resumes feminine

detail.label: Whole situation

runs.t: C'est intéressant. Il est intéressant.

comment: That is interesting [the situation/idea]. He/it is interesting [identified masculine referent]. Context determines the reference.

detail.label: Existence and negation

runs.t: Il y a des livres. Il n'y a pas de livres.

comment: There are books. There are no books. Use the same
frame for singular and plural.

detail.label: Presentation

runs.t: Voici votre billet. Voilà les autres voyageurs.

comment: Here is your ticket. There are the other travellers.
point out or present.

detail.label: Register

runs.t: Ce sont mes voisins. C'est mes voisins.

comment: They are my neighbours. The second is common in informal speech;
is the standard plural written model.

direct-objects.title: Him, her, it, them: direct objects
direct-objects.lead: A direct object is selected without a preposition in the French verb frame. Replace it with the matching pronoun before the verb it belongs to.

detail.label: Finite/compound

runs.t: Je le prends. Je l'ai pris.

comment: I take it [masculine]. I took it. The pronoun comes before
or auxiliary

detail.label: Negation

runs.t: Je ne la vois pas. Je ne veux pas la voir.

comment: I don’t see her. I don’t want to see her. The pronoun stays with the verb whose object it is.

detail.label: Imperative

runs.t: Prends-le. Ne le prends pas.

comment: Take it. Don’t take it. Positive commands attach with a hyphen; negative commands use normal pre-verb position.

detail.label: Gender of things

runs.t: La clé ? Je la cherche. Le sac ? Je le cherche.

comment: The key? I’m looking for it. The bag? I’m looking for it. French uses noun gender even for things.

detail.label: Earlier object agreement

runs.t: Les clés ? Je les ai trouvées.

comment: The keys? I found them. Earlier feminine plural COD triggers
: find).

detail.label: French frame, not English preposition

runs.t: J’écoute la radio. Je l’écoute.

comment: I listen to the radio. I listen to it.
is direct in French although English uses “to”.

indirect-objects.title: To him/her/them: indirect objects
indirect-objects.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: With selected French verbs,

runs.t: à

runs: + a person becomes an indirect object pronoun.

runs.t: lui

runs: means to him or to her;

runs.t: leur

runs: means to them.

detail.label: Compound position

runs.t: Je leur ai téléphoné.

comment: I phoned them.
precedes the auxiliary.
does not agree with this indirect object.

detail.label: Commands

runs.t: Parle-lui. Ne lui parle pas.

comment: Speak to him/her. Don’t speak to him/her. Positive command puts the pronoun after the verb.

detail.label: Counterexample

runs.t: Je pense à elle. Je m’intéresse à lui.

comment: I’m thinking about her. I’m interested in him. These frames retain
+ stressed pronoun for a person.

detail.label: English interference

runs.t: Je l’écoute. Je lui réponds.

comment: I listen to him/her. I answer him/her.
is direct;
a person is indirect.

detail.label: Plural versus possessive

runs.t: Je leur donne leurs clés.

comment: I give them their keys. Pre-verb
has no s; possessive
agrees with plural

pronoun-y.title: There or a thing: the place/complement pronoun
pronoun-y.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule

runs.t: Y

runs: can replace a place phrase or the

runs.t: à

runs: -complement of selected verbs when it refers to a thing or idea. It goes before its verb, except in positive commands.

detail.label: Different places

runs.t: Je suis dans le jardin. J’y suis.

comment: I am in the garden. I am there.
can replace a location introduced by
, not only

detail.label: A thing versus a person

runs.t: Je pense au voyage. J’y pense. Je pense à Léa. Je pense à elle.

comment: I’m thinking about the trip / it. I’m thinking about Léa / her. The personal complement uses a stressed pronoun.

detail.label: Governed complement

runs.t: Il participe au projet. Il y participe.

comment: He participates in the project. He participates in it. Learn
with its complement.

detail.label: Compound negation

runs.t: Je n'y suis jamais allé.

comment: I have never been there [masculine speaker].
precedes the auxiliary; agreement in
comes from the subject with
, not

detail.label: Boundary

runs.t: Y

runs: is not a substitute for every English “there” or every noun after

runs.t: à

runs: . Identify the French place/complement frame before replacing it.

en.title: Some, how many, about it: the amount/topic pronoun
en.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule

runs.t: En

runs: replaces an amount introduced by a partitive/indefinite/quantity frame, or a

runs.t: de

runs: -complement of selected verbs. Keep an explicit number or measure.

detail.label: Quantity remains

runs.t: J'ai beaucoup de travail. J'en ai beaucoup.

comment: I have a lot of work. I have a lot [of it]. Keep
after replacing the noun phrase.

detail.label: Measure remains

runs.t: Je prends une tranche de pain. J’en prends une tranche.

comment: I take a slice of bread. I take a slice [of it]. The measure remains.

detail.label: Negative

runs.t: Je n'en veux pas.

comment: I don’t want any.
precedes
follows the finite verb.

detail.label: A selected complement or departure

runs.t: J’ai besoin de ce document. J’en ai besoin. Je reviens de Lyon. J’en reviens.

comment: I need this document / it. I’m returning from Lyon / there. These meanings are selected by the frame.

detail.label: Person contrast

runs.t: Je parle de Léa. Je parle d’elle.

comment: I’m talking about Léa. I’m talking about her. Use a stressed personal complement in this bounded model.

detail.label: Command and common agreement

runs.t: Prends-en deux. J’en ai acheté deux.

comment: Take two. I bought two [of them].
follows a positive command; the participle stays unchanged in this common quantitative frame.

pronoun-order.title: Two object pronouns: order
pronoun-order.lead: Ordinary pre-verb order uses the sequence below. Choose a legal combination for the meaning, not one item from every group.

detail.label: Person difference

runs.t: Il me la montre. Il la leur montre.

comment: He shows it [feminine] to me. He shows it to them.
precedes
, but
follows

detail.label: Quantity pair

runs.t: Elle m’en donne deux. Donne-m’en deux.

comment: She gives me two [of them]. Give me two.
becomes
before
even in the positive command.

detail.label: Place and quantity

runs.t: Il y en a trois.

comment: There are three [of them].
precedes
in this fixed existence frame.

detail.label: Compound agreement

runs.t: Les clés ? Elle me les a données.

comment: The keys? She gave them to me.
is the earlier feminine plural direct object;
agrees with it.

detail.label: Negative command

runs.t: Ne le lui dis pas. Dis-le-lui.

comment: Don’t tell him/her that. Tell him/her that. The first is negative pre-verb order; the second is positive command order.

detail.label: Boundary
runs: Do not stack incompatible pronouns. The listed frames teach common two-pronoun combinations; longer idiomatic strings need separate checking.

possessive-pronouns.title: Mine, yours, his, hers
possessive-pronouns.lead: Replace a noun with a possessive pronoun. Choose the owner and match the gender/number of the thing possessed; keep the article.

detail.label: Singular and plural

runs.t: Mon sac est rouge. Le mien est rouge. Mes clés sont ici. Les miennes sont ici.

comment: My bag is red / Mine is red. My keys are here / Mine are here. The pronoun replaces the whole possessed noun phrase.

detail.label: Feminine forms

runs.t: la tienne / la sienne / la nôtre / la vôtre / la leur

comment: yours [familiar] / his or hers / ours / yours [polite/plural] / theirs, with a feminine singular referent.

detail.label: Plural owner forms

runs.t: les miens / les tiens / les siens ; les miennes / les tiennes / les siennes

comment: mine/yours/his-or-hers: masculine plural; then feminine plural. Owner and noun number are separate choices.

detail.label: Contractions

runs.t: Je pense à mes enfants. Et vous, aux vôtres ?

comment: I’m thinking of my children. And you, of yours?
contracts to

detail.label: Another possession frame

runs.t: Ce livre est à moi. C'est le mien.

comment: This book belongs to me. It’s mine.
+ stressed pronoun is another way to express ownership.

demonstrative-pronouns.title: This one, that one, that idea
demonstrative-pronouns.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Use demonstrative pronouns without repeating a noun.

runs.t: Celui/celle/ceux/celles

runs: match a specific noun;

runs.t: ça
cela

runs: can refer to a situation or idea.

detail.label: With a possessor

runs.t: Mon sac est noir. Celui de Léa est rouge.

comment: My bag is black. Léa’s is red.
replaces a masculine singular

detail.label: With relative

runs.t: Je prends celle qui est sur la table.

comment: I’ll take the one that is on the table [feminine referent].
introduces the completing relative clause.

detail.label: Object relative

runs.t: Les livres ? Je préfère ceux que tu as choisis.

comment: The books? I prefer the ones you chose.
replaces masculine plural

detail.label: Idea without noun gender

runs.t: Ça me plaît. Cela me semble utile.

comment: I like that. That seems useful to me.
refer to an idea or situation rather than matching a named noun.

detail.label: Entry depths
runs: Conversational

runs.t: ça

runs: is an early A1 recognition/use item. The A2 replacement forms and bounded B1

runs.t: de

runs: /relative completions build the fuller system; the card badge marks that main form family.

indefinite-pronouns.title: Someone, each one, several
indefinite-pronouns.lead: An indefinite pronoun stands for a person or thing without identifying it exactly. Distinguish it from a determiner followed by a noun.

detail.label: Determiner or pronoun

runs.t: Chaque personne choisit. Chacun choisit. Quelques personnes restent. Quelques-unes restent.

comment: Each person chooses / Each one chooses. A few people stay / A few stay [feminine].

detail.label: With adjective

runs.t: J’ai rencontré quelqu’un de gentil. Il y a quelque chose d’important.

comment: I met someone nice. There is something important.
links the adjective after

detail.label: Negative counterpart

runs.t: Quelqu’un arrive. Personne n’arrive.

comment: Someone is arriving. Nobody is arriving. The negative subject uses

detail.label: Singular everything

runs.t: Tout est prêt. Toutes sont prêtes.

comment: Everything is ready. All of them [feminine] are ready.
as everything stays singular; plural
agrees with its referents.

detail.label: Selection

runs.t: Certains sont utiles, d’autres non.

comment: Some are useful, others are not. The group is supplied by context.

exclamations.title: What a…! How…!
exclamations.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Use

runs.t: quel

runs: + noun to exclaim about a thing, agreeing with the noun.

runs.t: Comme
que

runs: can introduce a fuller exclamation about degree.

detail.label: Question or exclamation

runs.t: Quelle idée proposes-tu ? Quelle idée !

comment: What idea do you propose? What an idea! Context and punctuation distinguish the use.

detail.label: Plural agreement

runs.t: Quels grands arbres ! Quelles petites maisons !

comment: What tall trees! What small houses! Adjective and
agree with the noun.

detail.label: Full clause

runs.t: Comme elle parle bien ! Qu’elle parle bien !

comment: How well she speaks! Both patterns express degree in a complete clause.

detail.label: Register
runs: These are useful conventional exclamations, not a general rule for translating every English “how” question; interrogative how is usually

runs.t: comment

place-prepositions.title: At, to, in, from — place
place-prepositions.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Choose the French place frame, not a single English equivalent.

runs.t: à
de

runs: contract with

runs.t: le
les

runs: ; cities and countries have different patterns.

detail.label: Countries and origin

runs.t: en France / de France ; au Canada / du Canada ; aux États-Unis / des États-Unis

comment: in/to and from France [feminine], Canada [masculine], the United States [plural]. Masculine vowel-initial Iran uses

detail.label: House or person’s place

runs.t: Je suis chez le médecin. Je suis dans la salle.

comment: I am at the doctor’s. I am inside the room.
refers to a person/professional’s premises;
locates something inside.

detail.label: No contraction

runs.t: à la banque ; à l’école ; de la gare ; de l’hôtel

comment: at/to the bank; at/to school; from the station; from the hotel.
remain distinct.

detail.label: Nearby

runs.t: près de la gare ; à proximité du parc ; au bord du lac

comment: near the station; close to the park; at the edge of the lake.
contracts inside a longer place phrase too.

detail.label: Above and below

runs.t: en haut ; en bas ; sur la table ; sous la table

comment: upstairs/at the top; downstairs/at the bottom; on the table; under the table. Adverbial
need no following object.

detail.label: Route and means

runs.t: Je passe par Lyon. Je voyage en train. Je viens à pied.

comment: I go via Lyon. I travel by train. I come on foot.
marks a route here;
belong to selected transport frames.

detail.label: Companion or possession

runs.t: avec Léa ; chez elle

comment: with Léa; at her place.
and
answer different relationship questions.

detail.label: Naming exceptions
runs: Some islands and exceptional geographic names use different articles/prepositions. This finite set is a retrieval guide; verify an unfamiliar name rather than generalizing from spelling alone.

time-expressions.title: Since, for, ago, in — time
time-expressions.lead: First choose the time relationship: continuing duration, bounded duration, elapsed time or a future interval. English “for” is not one French preposition.

detail.label: Finished versus continuing

runs.t: J'ai attendu pendant une heure. J'attends depuis une heure.

comment: I waited for an hour [bounded]. I have been waiting for an hour [still waiting].

detail.label: Duration versus completion

runs.t: Il a travaillé pendant deux heures. Il a fini en deux heures.

comment: He worked for two hours. He finished in two hours.
measures time to the endpoint.

detail.label: Past reference point

runs.t: J’attendais depuis une heure quand elle est arrivée.

comment: I had been waiting for an hour when she arrived.
continues the situation at a past reference point.

detail.label: Planned stay

runs.t: Je pars pour une semaine.

comment: I’m going away for a week.
can mark an intended stay with departure/travel frames; it is not every duration’s default.

detail.label: Starting point

runs.t: À partir de lundi, je travaille ici. Dès lundi, je commence.

comment: From Monday onward, I work here. Starting/as early as Monday, I begin.
can emphasize the starting point.

detail.label: Deadline and approximation

runs.t: Je répondrai d’ici vendredi. Elle arrive vers huit heures.

comment: I’ll reply by Friday. She arrives around eight.
sets a horizon;
approximates a time.

detail.label: Relative days

runs.t: Il est arrivé mardi. La veille, il était à Lyon. Le lendemain, il est parti.

comment: He arrived Tuesday. The day before, he was in Lyon. The next day, he left.
relate to a reference day, not necessarily today.

detail.label: Time adverbs

runs.t: maintenant / bientôt / demain ; autrefois / aussitôt / récemment

comment: now / soon / tomorrow; formerly / immediately / recently. These contextual time clues do not mechanically choose a tense.

detail.label: As soon as

runs.t: Dès que tu arriveras, appelle-moi.

comment: As soon as you arrive, call me. A future-time
clause uses future French where English uses present.

verb-prepositions.title: A linking preposition — or none?
verb-prepositions.lead: Learn a verb/adjective with its complement frame and meaning. English “to” or “about” cannot predict the French preposition.

detail.label: First infinitive pattern

runs.t: apprendre à conduire ; réussir à finir ; aider à préparer

comment: learn to drive; manage to finish; help to prepare. Learn the infinitive partner with

detail.label: Second infinitive pattern

runs.t: décider de partir ; oublier de répondre ; refuser de venir

comment: decide to leave; forget to reply; refuse to come.
elides before a vowel.

detail.label: Adjective partners

runs.t: différent de moi ; content de toi ; prêt à partir ; fort en maths

comment: different from me; pleased with you; ready to leave; good at maths. Each adjective selects its own relation.

detail.label: Thing versus person replacement

runs.t: Je pense au projet. J’y pense. Je pense à elle.

comment: I’m thinking about the project / it. I’m thinking about her. Pronoun choice depends on the French frame and the kind of referent.

detail.label: Meaning contrast

runs.t: Je pense à partir. Je pense partir demain.

comment: I’m thinking of leaving. I think/intend to leave tomorrow. The frame changes the meaning.

detail.label: Boundary
runs: This card covers selected common noun/infinitive complements. It does not inventory every pronominal/idiomatic verb or guarantee that one verb always takes one preposition.

core-relatives.title: Subject, object, place: link two ideas
core-relatives.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: A relative clause describes a noun. Choose

runs.t: qui

runs: for its missing subject,

runs.t: que

runs: for its missing direct object, and

runs.t: où

runs: for place/time.

detail.label: Thing as subject

runs.t: Le train qui arrive est plein.

comment: The train that is arriving is full.
can refer to a thing because it is the relative-clause subject.

detail.label: Person as object

runs.t: La personne que je connais est ici.

comment: The person I know is here.
can refer to a person because it is the direct object.

detail.label: Elision and agreement

runs.t: Les clés qu'elle a trouvées sont ici.

comment: The keys she found are here.
; preceding feminine plural direct object triggers

detail.label: No duplicate subject/object

runs.t: La femme qui parle est ma sœur.

comment: The woman who is speaking is my sister. Do not add
inside the
clause;
already fills its subject role.

detail.label: Place/time

runs.t: C’est la maison où je suis né. C’est le soir où nous sommes partis.

comment: It’s the house where I was born [masculine speaker]. It’s the evening we left [masculine/mixed group].
can express place or time.

dont.title: Relatives for complements and possession
dont.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Use

runs.t: dont

runs: when the relative clause needs a simple

runs.t: de

runs: -complement, including possession. Identify that

runs.t: de

runs: relationship before choosing the pronoun.

detail.label: Recover the frame

runs.t: J’ai besoin de ce livre. Voici le livre dont j’ai besoin.

comment: I need this book. Here is the book I need.
includes the
relationship.

detail.label: Direct object contrast

runs.t: Le livre que je lis. Le livre dont je parle.

comment: The book I’m reading. The book I’m talking about.
is direct;
requires

detail.label: Possession

runs.t: C’est la femme dont le frère habite ici.

comment: It’s the woman whose brother lives here. Use
, not
, after
in this possession frame.

detail.label: Complex-preposition boundary

runs.t: la maison à côté de laquelle je travaille

comment: the house next to which I work.
is a whole preposition phrase; recognize
rather than substituting

detail.label: Boundary

runs.t: Dont

runs: is not every English “whose” construction and not every occurrence of

runs.t: de

runs: anywhere in a clause. This card teaches simple

runs.t: de

runs: complements and ordinary possession.

compound-relatives.title: Preposition + agreeing relative: recognition
compound-relatives.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Recognize a relative introduced by a preposition.

runs.t: Lequel

runs: forms agree with the noun they refer to; keep the preposition before the relative.

detail.label: Masculine referent

runs.t: le projet auquel je participe

comment: the project I participate in.
selects
contracts to

detail.label: Feminine referent

runs.t: la méthode avec laquelle elle travaille

comment: the method she works with.
+ feminine
stays separate.

detail.label: Plural referent

runs.t: les documents sur lesquels je travaille

comment: the documents I am working on.
Masculine plural
gives

detail.label: Complex preposition

runs.t: le bâtiment à côté duquel je travaille

comment: the building next to which I work.
gives

detail.label: People and scope
runs: For people, preposition +

runs.t: qui

runs: is also common, such as

runs.t: avec
qui

runs: (with whom). The productive selection matrix is deliberately outside this recognition card; do not use the form list to generate every construction.

ce-relatives.title: What…: relatives without a named noun
ce-relatives.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: When no specific noun supplies an antecedent, use

runs.t: ce

runs: + the relative matching the missing role. These forms can also frame an emphasis with

runs.t: c’est

detail.label: Subject versus object

runs.t: Je comprends ce qui se passe. Je comprends ce que tu dis.

comment: I understand what is happening. I understand what you’re saying. First
is the subject; second
is the object of

detail.label: Elision

runs.t: Dis-moi ce qu’elle veut.

comment: Tell me what she wants.
becomes
before

detail.label: De relation

runs.t: Ce dont j’ai besoin, c’est une réponse.

comment: What I need is an answer.
supplies the relation represented by
; the emphasized noun phrase identifies what is needed.

detail.label: Emphasis

runs.t: Ce que je veux dire, c’est que nous avons le temps.

comment: What I mean is that we have time. This frame emphasizes the content that follows.

detail.label: Whole preceding idea

runs.t: Elle vient demain, ce qui me fait plaisir.

comment: She is coming tomorrow, which makes me happy.
can refer to a whole preceding statement, not only a single noun.

si-patterns.title: If — or what if?
si-patterns.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: For a possible condition, use

runs.t: si

runs: + present with a present/future/command result. For an imagined present/future situation, use

runs.t: si

runs: + imperfect with conditional result.

detail.label: Likely future condition

runs.t: Si elle arrive tôt, nous partirons ensemble.

comment: If she arrives early, we’ll leave together. Present in the
clause, future in the result.

detail.label: Imagined situation

runs.t: Si nous habitions près de la mer, nous nagerions souvent.

comment: If we lived near the sea, we would swim often. Imperfect expresses the hypothesis, not past time here.

detail.label: Suggestion

runs.t: Et si nous prenions le train ?

comment: What if we took the train? No result clause is needed for this suggestion.

detail.label: Whether is different

runs.t: Je me demande s’il viendra.

comment: I wonder whether he will come.
is an indirect yes/no-question link here; future is possible.

detail.label: Not necessarily impossible
runs: An imperfect/conditional hypothesis can be imagined, uncertain or contrary to present fact. Do not label every such situation logically impossible.

detail.label: Boundary
runs: Past conditional and

runs.t: si

runs: + pluperfect counterfactual systems are outside this card even though narrative pluperfect is taught elsewhere.

reported-present.title: Report what someone says
reported-present.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: With a present reporting verb, use

runs.t: que

runs: for statements,

runs.t: si

runs: for yes/no questions and the question word for information questions. Adjust people and references to the reporting situation.

detail.label: Yes/no question

runs.t: Léa demande : « Tu viens ? » → Elle demande si tu viens.

comment: Léa asks, “Are you coming?” → She asks whether you’re coming.
means whether, not conditional if here.

detail.label: Who/where/when

runs.t: Il demande quand le train part.

comment: He asks when the train leaves. Keep the question word, with ordinary subject–verb order in this model.

detail.label: What, subject or object

runs.t: Elle demande ce qui se passe. Elle demande ce que tu veux.

comment: She asks what is happening. She asks what you want. Subject what →
; object what →

detail.label: Negative order

runs.t: Elle me demande de ne pas partir.

comment: She asks me not to leave.
+ negative infinitive reports the request.

detail.label: Reference changes

runs.t: Léa me dit : « Je te vois demain. » → Léa me dit qu’elle me voit demain.

comment: Léa says to me, “I’ll see you tomorrow.” → Léa tells me she’ll see me tomorrow. With immediate reporting, tomorrow can keep its reference.

detail.label: Boundary
runs: Do not infer an “always backshift” rule for other frames. Past reporting, shifted dates and retained-present/general-truth exceptions need a separate reviewed unit.

contrast.title: But, whereas, on the contrary
contrast.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Use

runs.t: mais

runs: for a contrast,

runs.t: alors que

runs: to connect contrasting clauses, and

runs.t: au contraire

runs: to oppose or correct an idea.

detail.label: Basic contrast

runs.t: Il fait froid, mais il y a du soleil.

comment: It’s cold, but it’s sunny.

detail.label: Opposed choices

runs.t: Elle veut partir, alors que je veux rester.

comment: She wants to leave, whereas I want to stay.
introduces a full clause.

detail.label: Correcting an assumption

runs.t: Ce n'est pas difficile. Au contraire, c'est très simple.

comment: It isn’t difficult. On the contrary, it’s very simple. The second statement reverses the expected judgment.

detail.label: Temporal reading

runs.t: Le téléphone a sonné alors que je lisais.

comment: The phone rang while I was reading. Here
relates times rather than opposing preferences.

purpose.title: To do — or so someone does
purpose.lead: Check the forms, meanings and limits below.

detail.label: Core rule
runs: Express an aim with

runs.t: pour

runs: + noun/infinitive. A separate expressed actor can use

runs.t: pour que
afin que

runs: + present subjunctive.

detail.label: Same actor

runs.t: Je pars tôt pour arriver à l’heure.

comment: I leave early to arrive on time. I both leave and arrive.

detail.label: Different actor

runs.t: Je laisse la porte ouverte pour que tu puisses entrer.

comment: I leave the door open so you can come in.
takes subjunctive

detail.label: More formal infinitive

runs.t: Nous réservons afin de payer moins cher.

comment: We book in order to pay less.
is a more formal aim link;
remains infinitive.

detail.label: Negative aim

runs.t: Je note la date pour ne pas l’oublier.

comment: I note the date so as not to forget it.
precedes the infinitive;
belongs before

detail.label: Purpose, not result
runs: Purpose states an intention; it does not claim the aim was achieved. A consequence linker states what follows, rather than what was intended.

cause.title: Because — or because of?
cause.lead: Choose a cause clause or a cause noun phrase. Other cause links can signal a shared reason, an explanation or a favourable cause.

detail.label: Clause versus noun

runs.t: Le train est en retard parce qu’il neige. Le train est en retard à cause de la neige.

comment: The train is late because it’s snowing / because of the snow.

detail.label: Favourable cause

runs.t: Grâce à ton aide, nous avons fini.

comment: Thanks to your help, we finished.
+ noun makes a favourable cause phrase.

detail.label: Shared reason

runs.t: Puisque tu es ici, aide-moi.

comment: Since you’re here, help me. The reason is treated as shared/available.

detail.label: Cause first

runs.t: Comme il pleut, nous restons ici.

comment: As it’s raining, we’re staying here. Causal
commonly starts the sentence.

detail.label: Explanation

runs.t: Je rentre, car je suis fatigué.

comment: I’m going home, because I’m tired [masculine speaker].
coordinates an explanation and is more characteristic of writing.

detail.label: Supporting explanation

runs.t: Il connaît bien la ville. En effet, il y habite depuis dix ans.

comment: He knows the town well. Indeed, he has lived there for ten years.
supports the preceding statement.

result.title: So, therefore, that’s why
result.lead: A result linker presents the consequence of the preceding situation. It points from the reason to what follows.

detail.label: Reason first

runs.t: Le train est annulé. C’est pour ça que je prends le bus.

comment: The train is cancelled. That’s why I’m taking the bus.
introduces a following clause.

detail.label: Written alternative

runs.t: Il pleut. C’est pourquoi nous restons ici.

comment: It’s raining. That’s why we’re staying here. No extra
after
in this pattern.

detail.label: Formal consequence

runs.t: Le dossier est incomplet. Par conséquent, la demande est refusée.

comment: The file is incomplete. Consequently, the application is refused.

detail.label: Consequence versus sequence

runs.t: Elle a ouvert la porte et le chien est sorti. Puis elle a fermé la porte.

comment: She opened the door and the dog went out. Then she closed the door.
can connect a natural result;
sequences events.

detail.label: Causal inventory overlap
runs: A source may list a connective near cause vocabulary. Classify

runs.t: c’est pourquoi

runs: by its actual consequence meaning so the learner sees the direction clearly.

sequence.title: Add, order & conclude
sequence.lead: Choose a link for addition, alternatives, continuation, chronological order or conclusion. A short connector inventory stays tied to a clear sentence frame.

detail.label: Addition and alternative

runs.t: Tu prends le train ou le bus ? Léa prend le train et le métro.

comment: Are you taking the train or the bus? Léa takes the train and the metro.

detail.label: Add a point

runs.t: Il est rapide. En plus, il est peu cher.

comment: It’s fast. In addition, it’s inexpensive.
adds an argument.

detail.label: Also position

runs.t: Elle vient aussi. Il vient également.

comment: She is coming too. He is also coming. These adverbs sit inside an ordinary statement; formal sentence-initial
has other syntax outside this card.

detail.label: Numbered order

runs.t: Premièrement, lisez. Deuxièmement, répondez.

comment: Firstly, read. Secondly, answer. The sequence words do not change verb conjugation.

detail.label: Continuation or repetition

runs.t: Il travaille encore. Il revient encore. Il veut encore du pain.

comment: He is still working. He is coming back again. He wants more bread. Context chooses the meaning of

detail.label: Concluding outcome

runs.t: Finalement, nous sommes restés. À la fin du film, nous sommes partis.

comment: In the end, we stayed. At the end of the film, we left. finally/outcome differs from a location at the end of a period.

detail.label: And then

runs.t: Nous avons mangé, et puis nous sommes partis.

comment: We ate, and then we left.
combines addition and sequence;
can also mean then/so according to context.

concession.title: Despite, although, yet
concession.lead: A concession keeps a fact while opposing its expected result. Choose a noun phrase, a finite clause or an adverbial link.

detail.label: Noun versus clause

runs.t: Malgré la pluie, nous sortons. Bien qu’il pleuve, nous sortons.

comment: Despite the rain, we’re going out. Although it’s raining, we’re going out.
is subjunctive of

detail.label: Expected result reversed

runs.t: Il pleut. Pourtant, nous sortons.

comment: It’s raining. Yet we’re going out.
links statements without becoming a conjunction followed by

detail.label: Same actor possible

runs.t: Elle travaille bien qu’elle soit fatiguée.

comment: She works although she is tired. The same actor does not remove the subjunctive after

detail.label: Conversational concession

runs.t: Il pleut, mais on sort quand même.

comment: It’s raining, but we’re going out anyway.
acknowledges the obstacle.

detail.label: However

runs.t: Le trajet est long. Cependant, il est agréable.

comment: The journey is long. However, it is pleasant. A concessive adverb can begin a separate sentence.
